headline: Philippine Peso Closes at ₱61.815 Against US Dollar, Near Historic Low
seoTitle: Peso Closes at ₱61.815/$1 Near Record Low | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine peso closed at ₱61.815 against the US dollar on August 19, near a historic low, as oil-price pressure and domestic weather disruptions weighed on markets.
deck: The local currency lost three centavos from the previous session as higher global oil prices and domestic weather disruptions added pressure.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine peso closed at ₱61.815 against the US dollar on Wednesday, August 19, according to the approved FMB News overnight package citing Bankers Association of the Philippines spot-market data.
That was three centavos weaker than Tuesday's ₱61.785 close. The package reports total spot trading volume of $1.14 billion and describes the finish as the currency's second-weakest on record.

sections.heading: Context · What's driving the move
paragraphs: Market commentary cited in the package points to higher international crude-oil prices and domestic supply-chain disruption from prolonged monsoon rains as pressures on the peso.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A weaker peso can raise the local-currency cost of imported fuel, food and other goods, although it also increases the peso value of dollar-denominated remittances when converted locally.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Markets will be watching oil prices, domestic weather conditions, dollar demand and any Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas signals on excessive foreign-exchange volatility.
